case_study: The Boeing 737 MAX: MCAS and Automation Authority

reflection_1_who_has_the_last_word.principle: The human engineer maintains 100% unconditional authority and legal/production responsibility. The AI has zero decision-making sovereignty.
reflection_1_who_has_the_last_word.response_to_uncertainty: Never accept code under the rationalization that 'the AI probably knows something I don't.' When an instinct signals something is amiss, pause immediately. Do not merge. Deconstruct the logic, write an adversarial black-box test, or isolate the function in a scratch script until the exact invariant is proven. If you cannot defend the code under SEV1 postmortem grilling, you do not ship it.

reflection_2_the_single_point_of_failure.identification: The single point of failure is the fatigued, over-trusting human reviewer skimming diffs at the end of the day.
reflection_2_the_single_point_of_failure.analysis: Just as MCAS trusted a single un-redundant sensor to override experienced pilots, an engineering team that relies on a single tired reviewer trusting a green test suite creates a single point of catastrophic failure. Superficial tests often verify only the happy path, masking critical IDOR, race conditions, and unhandled exceptions.
systemic_interlocks: Automated CI Security Scanners: Linters and SAST tools that enforce security rules out-of-band.
Multi-Reviewer Governance: Mandatory two-human peer approvals for data mutation and auth boundaries.
Black-Box Behavioral Invariants: Requiring negative test cases (unauthenticated 401, unauthorized 403, duplicate 409) before any pull request is merged.
